result.unit: ch1 cold open and first teasers (0:00-0:30)
result.summary:
Technically the unit is clean. Every marker-synced event lands 2-3 frames before its word, and the cuts at 7.71, 16.24 and 18.80 s are clean, with no black, empty or glitched frames and no static hold over 3 s. All on-screen text is in the script's onscreen list and is 5 words or fewer. The flat-map teaser, the north/south data beat and the coin crack are strong. The problems sit in the two places that matter most for retention: the first 8 seconds and Explorer gag 1.
(1) Frame 0 matches none of the three thumbnails. Thumbnail C, which metadata.md describes as matching the first second, was rendered with a camera 36 deg further west.
(2) The globe barely moves on "Spin a globe".
(3) South America and India are slivers on the globe's edge, so "South America ... India" does not read; only Africa does.
(4) The yellow "?" ring, the hook's focal point, sits at 86-97% of frame height, in the caption and progress-bar zone.
(5) The gag's catch-and-wobble punchline is lost. The drop exits through the bottom of the frame and the Explorer stands idle for about 1.1 s.
Reworking the camera keys of the single cold-open globe shot in ch1.js would fix four of these. The rest is polish.
strengths: Marker sync is exact throughout. Each event leads its word by 2-3 frames: arcs 2.91 s ('melting' 2.99); South America, Africa and India re-light at 3.85/5.29/6.61 s (3.93/5.37/6.69); Greenland cut 7.71 s (7.78); Florida, Baja and Kamchatka pop at 9.10/9.90/10.90 s; drip arrows 13.74 s (13.84); north overlay 18.78 s (18.88); equator 20.94 s (21.04); city dots 22.78 s (22.88); coin 27.26 s (27.36); crack 29.32 s (29.30).
Clean hard cuts at 7.71, 16.24 and 18.80 s. No black, empty or broken frames, and no static hold over 3 s.

The Equal Earth flat map (7.7-16.2 s) is the unit's best image. Hero-orange continents with white outlines, one leader-line pill at a time (GREENLAND, FLORIDA, BAJA, KAMCHATKA, each on the right tip), then seven yellow drip arrows. It reads instantly, it is on-palette, and it is the closest match to thumbnails A and B.

The data beat (18.8-24.7 s) explains two numbers with almost no text: an orange north-land overlay, an equator draw-on, a split bar with no digits, and city dots scaled by the square root of population. Facts are correct (68% of land north; about 9 in 10 people). Pills are 4-5 words, in the onscreen list and above the bottom 12%.
The coin beat works as a visual joke. A generic coin spins up on 'coincidence', then freezes and cracks on 'not', and Africa shows through the split.
The Explorer reads well: about 45% of frame height, with a warm key light and a rim light. The sun flare sells 'July', and cutting on 'dashboard' rather than 'July' gives the gag a usable 2.56 s.

issues.problem: Frame 1 is not the thumbnail in motion, for any of the three Test & Compare thumbnails. A and B (B is the primary per deliver/ep01/metadata.md) are the flat Equal Earth map with South America, Africa and India large, and three white arrows into a big '?' ring. C is labelled in metadata.md as 'globe in the cold-open look, so it matches the first second', but it is centred on South America with Africa on the right edge. The film's frame 0 is centred on Africa: South America is an edge sliver, India is not visible, there are no arrows, and the '?' ring is about 85 px wide versus about 200 px in the thumbnails. A viewer who clicked any of the three sees a different picture at 0:00, and the B-style image arrives only at 7.7 s.
issues.evidence: full/x_000.000.jpg compared with thumbs/final/thumb_C_they_point_here.jpg in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/wf/u1_cold_open/cmp_thumbC_vs_f0.jpg. thumbs.js line 139 renders C with {lat:-28, lon:-24, alt:2.55, lookOffset:[-0.12,-0.07]}. The ch1.js cold-open keys are [{t:0, lat:-29, lon:12, alt:3.05}, {t:8, lat:-31, lon:30, alt:2.8}]: a 36 deg longitude mismatch.
issues.fix: In ch1.js, cold-open G() (t0:0 to t.grl-0.07), start on the thumbnail-C framing: first key {t:0, lat:-28, lon:-24, alt:2.9} (2.55 if the top crop is acceptable) plus sun:{lookOffset:[0,-0.06]}. globeShot merges o.sun into the camera state passed to drawGlobe, so this works. Continue with the camera path in the South America/India issue. Alternatively, re-render thumbnail C from the film's actual frame 0 and put C first in the test. Either way, correct the metadata.md claim.

issues.problem: Of 'South America. Africa. India.', only Africa reads. South America is a thin crescent along the left limb. Its re-light at 3.87 s comes 0.1 s after the 3.74 s dim, so it looks like a flicker rather than a beat. On 'India' (6.69 s), a sliver of about 20 px lights up on the far right limb. The Kanyakumari arc runs down the limb like an orbit line, not a drip. The three-continent pattern, the core claim of the video, is not visible until the flat map at 7.7 s.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/wf/u1_cold_open/crop_sam.jpg (3.57, 3.77, 3.83, 3.87, 4.00, 4.33 s): bright, dim, dim, bright crescent on the limb. crop_ind.jpg (6.50-7.30 s): India only an edge sliver with the marker at the limb. full/x_007.500.jpg shows the whole composition: Africa central, the other two at the limbs. From camera lat -30/lon 20, India's centre is about 75 deg from the view centre, at the horizon.
issues.fix: Make the globe actually spin through the list. In the cold-open G() in ch1.js, replace the two keys with [{t:0, lat:-28, lon:-24, alt:2.9}, {t:t.afr-0.3, lat:-28, lon:-8, alt:2.9, ease:E.inOutSine}, {t:t.ind-0.2, lat:-22, lon:52, alt:3.0, ease:E.inOutExpo}, {t:t.grl, lat:-22, lon:56, alt:3.0}]. South America and Africa are then both on the disc for 'South America' and 'Africa' (centres about 57 and 38 deg from view centre), and a whip to lon 52 puts India and Africa on the disc for 'India'. Move the coldAlpha dim to prog(tt, t.melt+0.1, t.melt+0.4) so South America is visibly dim for about 0.5 s before it snaps back. Add whoosh_soft (-14) on the whip.

issues.problem: The hook's focal point sits in the bottom 12% of the frame and crosses title-safe. The yellow ring with the white '?' at the South Pole, where all three arcs converge, sits at the bottom edge for the whole cold open. That is exactly where YouTube draws uploaded captions (captions_en.srt ships with the video, and muted feed autoplay shows captions) and the progress bar and controls. The ring is also small (r=40, about 85 px), so on a phone the 'unresolved question' is a tiny yellow circle at the bottom edge.
issues.evidence: Yellow-pixel measurement on exact frames: ring spans y 931-1015 (86-94% of height) at 0 s, 940-1029 at 4 s and 957-1044 (88.6-96.7%) at 7.67 s. It crosses the 95% title-safe line from about 4 s. See full/x_000.000.jpg and full/x_007.500.jpg. Thumbnail C draws the same ring with RR=104 and a 150 px '?' (thumbs.js lines 141-142).
issues.fix: In the cold-open G() in ch1.js, add sun:{lookOffset:[0,-0.06]}. This tilts the view so the globe rises about 106 px (1766 px focal length x 0.06). Raise alt about 0.3 (3.05 to 3.35 and 2.8 to 3.1) so the globe still fits: radius about 417 px, centre about y 434. The pole then projects at about y 830-850 (77-79%). Raise poleRing(ctx, tt, {r:40}) to r:56. Apply the same lift to the s008 reprise of this look (31.9 s onward) so the payoff ring is not under the captions either.

issues.problem:
Explorer gag 1's punchline ('tries to catch the drip and nearly falls off Africa') does not land:
- The Interact reach is at chest height while the drop sits at his feet about 1 m away (17.0-17.5 s), so it never looks like a catch.
- The drop slides out through the bottom-right corner of the frame (17.5-17.6 s, cut off by the frame edge) instead of visibly falling off into space.
- The HitRecieve_2 'wobble' is only a slight lean at about 17.8 s.
- He then stands idle for about 1.1 s until the cut.
The cartoon_fall whistle at 17.54 s has no fall on screen to land on. The tiny planet's surface also does not read as Africa's tip, and the sphere-plus-cone drop shows a visible seam at 1080p.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/wf/u1_cold_open/gag_wobble.jpg (17.2-18.8 s every 0.1 s), full/x_017.200.jpg, x_017.600.jpg (drop cut by the frame bottom) and x_018.267.jpg (idle). Motion energy over 17.8-18.7 s is 1.1-1.7% of pixels changed per 0.5 s. Code: slide a1=0.98 puts the drop at about y_cam -1.5 against a half-height of 0.97 (below frame); the wobble amplitude is only 0.03 rad.
issues.fix:
In the ch1.js GAG 1 block:
1. Keep the fall in frame. Set a1 from 0.98 to 0.70, and launch the free-fall from there with tangential, slightly upward velocity so the drop tumbles off the planet's right limb into space while still on screen. Alternatively, retarget gst.lookFrom from [0,0.3,0.95] to [0,-0.15,1.45] with fov 34.
2. Make it a catch. Move the Explorer toward the drop during the reach (al 0.20 to 0.34 over G1+0.5 to G1+1.2) so his hand sweeps over the drop just as it slips.
3. Make the wobble read. From G1+1.6 to the cut, use an al oscillation of about 0.10 rad at about 3 Hz plus a ±15 deg pitch on hero.root. Play HitRecieve_2 and cue cartoon_fall at G1+1.6, and cut at G1e mid-wobble.
4. Optionally, tint the planet patch under his feet orange so it reads as the dripping continent, and build the drop from a LatheGeometry teardrop profile to remove the seam.

issues.problem: The narrator says 'Spin a globe', but the globe barely moves. Until the arcs start at 2.91 s, the only motion is a 2.25 deg/s drift and the small ring pulse. That gives a weak orienting response in the 3 seconds with the highest drop-off. The checklist asks for motion in the first 1-2 s, and the bench opening template says the globe should already be rotating.
issues.evidence: Motion energy between frames 0.5 s apart is a mean absolute difference of 2.0-2.3 levels, with about 4% of pixels changing by more than 12 levels. The camera move at 25.5-26.5 s scores about 18%. The cold-open keys go from lon 12 to 30 over 8 s.
issues.fix: This is covered by the camera path in the South America/India issue. If it is kept separate, add an eased spin of 30-40 deg over the first 1.5 s from the thumbnail framing (E.outExpo key at t=1.5), with the existing whoosh_soft at 0 doing the work, then settle into the slow drift.

issues.problem: Three labels break the 5% title-safe margin (96 px each side). The 'TWO-THIRDS OF ALL LAND' pill ends at x≈1870 (97.4% of width), and 'NEARLY 9 IN 10 OF US' at x≈1830. The BAJA pill's left edge is at x≈80 (4.2%).
issues.evidence: full/x_019.700.jpg and x_022.000.jpg (pill spans x 1390-1870 because BAR.x=1440 and BAR.w=380 centre the pill at 1630). full/x_023.900.jpg (pill reaches about 1830). full/x_010.400.jpg (BAJA pill spans x 80-197, with TIPFILL offset [-150,70] anchored right of the Cabo San Lucas tip at x≈347).
issues.fix: In the ch1.js s005 block, change BAR from {x:1440} to {x:1380}. The bar and both pills shift 60 px left, putting the pill's right edge at about 1810. In TIPFILL, change the BAJA offset from [-150,70] to [-125,70] (left edge about 105 px).

result.summary: The second half (57.9-75.3 s), the Bacon proof sequence, is strong. It uses the real 1620 pages (title page, Novum Organum p.239 with 'acuminati' and 'quod non temere accidit' underlined, the Parasceve card with 'x2'). Everything is synced 1-3 frames ahead of its words and nothing holds static. The teaser half (45-55 s) is weak. (1) The '4 MODELS' flash on 'crash' shows four present-day Earths instead of the planned four future end-states, so the ~1 s glimpse of the final reveal is missing. (2) At 68.9-69.33 the 'acuminati' underline is not clipped and hangs below the page on the bare desk. (3) The 1875 tetrahedron is framed so its Antarctica vertex runs off the bottom of the frame; its faces are nearly black and its 'yellow edges' are 1 px hairlines, so it reads as a dark flat triangle. Smaller fixes: the near-black dip at the grid cut, the '?' ring in the bottom 12 %, the English quote pill swapped out mid-quote, an 'x2' stamp too brief to read, and tiny cape markers. Note: the contact-sheet labels from the fps filter run a few frames late (the sheet's '45.00' cell is really about 45.1). All sync checks here used exact frames.
strengths: Marker sync is excellent on every beat (exact frames): X stamp pops 47.50 vs 'dead' 47.52; cut to the spinning globe 48.85 vs 'last' 48.92; title-page dissolve starts 57.88 vs 'Not' 58.08; portrait cut 61.87 vs 'Bacon' 61.90; page cut 64.83 vs 'narrow' 64.86; 'Africa' globe 69.35 vs 69.50; page cut 72.47 and 'quod non temere' underline starting 72.54 on 'not'.

The Bacon section is real show-don't-tell storytelling. The actual 1620 Instauratio Magna title page leads into the van Somer portrait and then Novum Organum p.239, with the exact Latin underlined ('acuminati', then 'quod non temere ac-/cidit'). The Parasceve card stamped 'X2' adds the second source, and the tilt-up reveals that the 'accident' sentence sits on the same page. It proves the title claim with primary sources by 1:13.
Archival look is consistent and premium: paper-bordered print frames with soft shadows on a wood desk, sepia grade, and a smooth Ken Burns from the galleon up to 'FRANCISCI DE VERULAMIO'.
The 2026 -> 1620 JetBrains Mono counter with the left-to-right sepia wipe over the seven-tips Equal Earth map is an elegant time-travel transition that also calls back the hook map.
The planned hard cut to black lands one frame before 'Eventually.' (53.10 vs 53.12) and sells the deadpan joke; the fade up from black is clean.
No static holds: a 0.5 s frame-difference scan finds nothing static except the planned 1.4 s black, and a visual event lands every ~1.5-3 s.
All on-screen text comes from the script's onscreen lists and stays at 7 words or fewer, with no subtitles, sources or emojis; the cold-open globe spins in Earth's true rotation direction.

issues.problem: The '4 MODELS' flash on 'the four continents your country might crash into' shows four PRESENT-DAY Earth globes from different angles, not the planned four future end-states. The viewer sees four ordinary Earths (Americas, Atlantic, Greenland, Hudson Bay) with a small white dot on Kansas. Nothing has crashed, there is no US fill, and the 1 s glimpse of the final reveal (retention checklist B) is missing. The '4 MODELS' label sits over four identical present-day Earths.
issues.evidence: Exact frame 52.70 at full res: tile 0 is today's North/South America and Atlantic with a white ring on Kansas, and tiles 1-3 show the same present-day geography from other angles. The ch1.js makeTiles() path renders api.drawGlobe of the present-day globe at views [[12,-60],[52,-140],[5,-125],[55,-55]]. The USOV overlay is not visible in any tile. The script's s010 plan calls for 'the four model end-state stills (pre-rendered in s099-s102)'.
issues.fix: Replace makeTiles() with ch6's end-state stills. ch6.js already builds them: holdFrame(m) / ensureStills() S[i].b for PANGAEA PROXIMA, NOVOPANGAEA, AMASIA and AURICA, already drawn with drawUS. Export them once to ep/ep01/img/model_end_0..3.jpg, either from a one-off still pass or by grabbing each MODELS[i].tShrink frame from the ch6 chunks once they are rendered. Load them through IM and drawImage them into the four tiles, keeping the existing hero/cyan/yellow/green borders (they already match MODELS[i].col) and the '4 MODELS' pill.

issues.problem: During the tilt-up on page n246, the orange 'acuminati' underline is not clipped to the print. It slides out of the page and hangs on the bare desk 30-40 px below the page edge for about 13 frames, a visible stray element on a calm shot.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 69.00/69.20/69.33: an orange line about 280 px wide at y≈884-895, while the print's bottom edge is at y≈855 (full-res crop of 69.20 shows it on the wood desk). Cause: X.printKB clips only the image inside its own save/restore and returns an unclipped mapper; the s013 tilt shot calls X.underline(ctx, m, BX.acum, 1, {alpha:0.7}) with no clip.
issues.fix: In the ch1.js s013 tilt shot (base t0: t.breath - 0.55), wrap the call: ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(PAGE_R[0], PAGE_R[1], PAGE_R[2], PAGE_R[3]); ctx.clip(); X.underline(...); ctx.restore(). Better, add an o.clip rect option to X.underline in ch1_fx.js and pass PAGE_R at every call site.

issues.problem: The 1875 tetrahedron reads as a dark flat triangle, not a 'pyramid Earth'. Its south vertex (Antarctica, the whole point of Green's theory) runs off the bottom of the frame for the entire morph and sits inside the bottom 12 %. The camera-facing Pacific face is nearly black. The 'yellow edges' are 1 px pale hairlines. After the snap-back, the sphere's top is clipped (47.7-48.5).
issues.evidence: Exact frames 46.6 and 47.2-47.5: the vertex is cut by the bottom edge, with Antarctica's white patch at y≈880-1080+. A full-res crop shows the edges as 1 px lines (WebGL LineBasicMaterial). Frame mean luma is about 17/255. Geometry: morph.js circumradius = R*1.55 = 3.41 (vertex at y≈-3.4), but the camera lookFrom([0,-0.8,9.6->8.6],[0,-0.25,0],32) only covers about y -2.85..+2.35. At 47.8 the globe top sits about 20 px above the frame edge.
issues.fix: In the ch1.js tetra base() (t0 TET0), animate the look target with k from [0,0,0] to [0,-1.15,0]. Raise and pull back the camera, for example dst.lookFrom([1.5, 2.0, lerp(11.2, 10.4, ...)], target, 32), so the top (Arctic) face shows and the 3D form reads, the vertex stays above y≈920 and the sphere top stays under the '1875' pill. Draw the edges in 2D after ctx.drawImage: project the 4 vertices (verts*2.2*1.55 through te.matrixWorld) with dst.project and stroke PAL.yellow at 5 px with alpha = edgeAlpha. Raise the stage key/exposure, or turn te so a lit continental edge faces the camera.

issues.problem: The English quote pill '"NARROW AND POINTED TOWARD THE SOUTH"', the line that proves the title, is fully legible for only about 0.8 s. It swaps to the Latin gloss at 65.86 while the narrator is still saying 'pointed toward the south' (65.70-67.34). All quote pills are small, about 30 px cap height, and their bottom edge sits on the 12 % line (y≈952), so a phone viewer and the mute test get very little of the key quote.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 64.833 (fading in), 65.2-65.7 (full) and 65.9 (gloss fading in). The code has pillT(..., t.narrow - 0.07, t.narrow + 1.0, {size:40}) at y=920. A full-res crop of the 73.6 pill shows the box at y≈888-952 with text cap height ≈30 px.
issues.fix: Move the swap from t.narrow + 1.0 to t.narrow + 1.9 (≈66.76, when the Parasceve 'acuminata' underline starts), so the English quote covers the spoken quote and the gloss pairs with the second 'acuminata'. Raise pill size 40->48 and y 920->880 for both s012 pills and the s013 'NOT TO BE ATTRIBUTED TO MERE ACCIDENT' pill.

issues.problem: The 'matching capes' do not pop. The cape markers at Cape Froward and Cape Agulhas are tiny orange dots that are barely visible on a phone. The white draw-on lines are full country borders, so the continents read as a busy political map instead of the signature clean white outline. The fill is a muddy brick red (alpha 0.5) rather than the hero orange.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 70.1-72.0: cape dots about 9 px radius at (≈640,900) and (≈1330,680). Internal African and South American borders are drawn (strokeProjected over R_SA/R_AF). coldSet([0.5,0.5,0]) gives the dull red. The plan asks for 'outlined white side by side, their southern capes pulsing orange'.
issues.fix: In the s013 G() shot, set tipMarkers r 9 -> 24 with a PAL.yellow ring and a larger pulse. Stroke coastline-only rings (continent outline) instead of the country rings R_SA/R_AF. Use coldSet([0.85,0.85,0]). Optionally push in slightly toward the South Atlantic so both capes sit closer to centre.

issues.problem: The cut from the bright spinning globe to the grid dips to near black for 3-4 frames, because the tiles fade in from alpha 0 with a stagger. The grid only fully lands at about 52.10, after 'crash' (51.84-52.08) has ended, so the hit word gets a dark blink instead of an impact.
issues.evidence: Per-frame mean luma (limited range, 16 = black): 30.7 at 51.77, 20.7 at 51.80, 21.0 at 51.83, 21.9 at 51.87, 23.1 at 51.90, back to 30.7 at 52.10. Exact frame 51.80 is almost black with a faint '4 MODELS' pill. Code: a = prog(lt, i*0.06, i*0.06+0.2).
issues.fix: Draw all tiles at full alpha from the first frame and stagger with a scale pop (1.08 -> 1.0 over 0.15 s) or a border flash instead, or start the ramp early: a = prog(lt + 0.15, i*0.04, i*0.04 + 0.12). This becomes moot if the shot is rebuilt with the ch6 stills, as long as they are drawn at full alpha from frame 1.

issues.problem: The yellow '?' pole ring (the recurring Antarctica mystery motif) sits at the very bottom of the frame, inside the bottom 12 % and outside the 5 % title-safe margin, where the YouTube scrub bar and controls cover it.
issues.evidence: Exact frames: ring centre at y≈993 (49.5) and y≈1025-1033 (51.2-51.77). A full-res crop at 51.6 shows the ring spanning y≈993-1075 of 1080.
issues.fix: In the s010 cold-open G() shot, frame the globe so the pole projects higher: keys lat -24 -> -18 become about -36 -> -30, or alt 2.9 -> 3.2, or apply a lookOffset of about -60 px. Keep the ring centre above y≈920 and check with a single still.

issues.problem: The 'he wrote it twice' beat is too brief to read. The Parasceve card slides in at 66.31 and the 'X2' stamp only completes at 67.46. Card and stamp then vanish in a single frame at 67.91, a pop-off cut back to the clean page 0.55 s before 'breath', so 'X2' is fully readable for only about 0.45 s.
issues.evidence: Exact frames: 67.40 shows the stamp still semi-transparent; 67.867 and 67.90 show card and X2 fully visible; 67.933 shows the plain page with no card. Code: P387 = t.narrow + 1.45; stamp at P387+0.95..1.15; shot ends at t.breath - 0.55.
issues.fix: Start the slide earlier, P387 = t.narrow + 1.0, with the stamp at P387 + 0.8, so the stamp holds about 1 s. Replace the pop-off with a 0.3 s slide-out to the right ending at t.breath - 0.55, or carry the card into the tilt shot and slide it out there.

result.unit: ch2 other side of the Earth, part 1 (3:00-4:30)
result.summary: This part is well paced and varied: diorama, 2D profiles, polar discs, globe, cut-away, tiny planet and flat map, with a scene change every 2-8 s, no black frames and no static hold over 3 s (measured). Most beats land 2-4 frames early, and the Kansas dig-and-pop-out gag chain is the best comedy so far. It is not shippable yet because of four blockers. First, the 'Arctic Ocean' shape is Natural Earth's central-basin label polygon (4.85 M km2 against Antarctica's 12.3 M km2). That makes both the 'sizes nearly match' beat and the chapter's first jaw-drop ('MOST OF ANTARCTICA: OPPOSITE THE ARCTIC OCEAN', only 37% yellow) contradict their own on-screen text. Second, Antarctica's orange fill shows through the globe onto Africa and Europe for about 1.4 s. Third, the mirrored-US proof never renders, because feat('United States of America') returns the Northern Mariana Islands. All three have small, concrete fixes: a new Arctic polygon, clampHidden=true, and feat('USA'). Both cut-away shots also crop off the poles, which removes the geographic anchor of 'straight through'. I expect about 8/10 once the blockers and the cut-away framing are fixed.
strengths: Sync is tight on most markers (checked on exact frames): profile cut 0.1 s before 'two', whip on 'bottom', ice rise exactly on 'up', shutter flash and inversion on 'photographic', 'CHINA?' completing on 'myth', China fill 3 frames before 'China', whip on 'test', Kansas marker and pill on 'Kansas', dig gag on 'dig', pop-out on 'southern', equator flash on 'hemisphere', FALSE stamp on the second 'China'.

The polar-disc 'photographic negatives' beat is a clean explainer. The Arctic disc inverts on the word, then reverts with a cyan glow while Antarctica glows warm, and the colour-coded 'OCEAN ON TOP. LAND AT BOTTOM.' headline sits over discs offset top and bottom.

The Kansas gag chain is the comedy high point and is well lit at a readable size (about 420 px). He digs, rides the drill head upside down through the core, rockets out of the water, tumbles, then treads water chest-deep with ripple rings.
Format variety and pacing are strong: no black frames, no hold over 3 s (frame-difference scan), and a meaningful visual event every 2-5 s.

Geography checks out where I verified it: the Kansas marker at the lower-48 centre, the Kansas antipode at 39.8S 81.4E, and the dashed line to Ile Saint-Paul at about 222 mi (so '200+' is correct). The equator line is correctly placed, and China's antipode lands over Chile and Argentina with about a quarter yellow.
On-screen text discipline is good: every headline and pill is from the onscreen list, at most 7 words, large condensed caps in dark pills, and the depth ruler counts land on the spoken numbers.

issues.problem: The shape dragged as 'the Arctic Ocean' is Natural Earth's central-basin label polygon (www/geo/arctic_ocean.geojson, 71-90N, a crude straight-edged hexagon), not the Arctic Ocean (about 14 M km2). Once it settles on Antarctica it covers only about 40% of it. Viewers see the sizes clearly NOT matching while the narration says 'the sizes nearly match' and the pill says 'ARCTIC OCEAN = ANTARCTICA (ALMOST)'. The same wrong shape is already outlined at 180.0 next to the NORTH POLE pill.
issues.evidence: Frame 212.5: the cyan shield covers the centre-right ~40% of the orange-outlined Antarctica. The Peninsula, the Weddell and Ross sides and most of East Antarctica are uncovered. Measured ring areas (Lambert equal-area): arctic_ocean.geojson 4.85 M km2 vs ne_50m Antarctica 12.26 M km2.
issues.fix: Replace www/geo/arctic_ocean.geojson (loaded in ch2.js: const ARC = await loadGeo('arctic_ocean')). Use a dissolved union of ne_10m_geography_marine_polys: Arctic Ocean, Barents, Kara, Laptev, East Siberian, Chukchi, Beaufort, The North Western Passages, Lincoln Sea, Greenland Sea, Baffin Bay (+ small gulfs). Measured union area is 11.9 M km2, against Antarctica's 12.3. Alternatively rasterize 'ocean north of 68N' from ne_50m_land (12.5 M km2). Re-render the 180.0 pole view, the s028 drag and the s029 top-down shot.

issues.problem: The first jaw-drop is visually false. With the undersized polygon the yellow overlap covers only ~37% of mirrored Antarctica. Most of the pink mirrored Antarctica visibly lands on the Canadian Arctic islands, Greenland and the Siberian coast, which is land. Meanwhile the pill reads 'MOST OF ANTARCTICA: OPPOSITE THE ARCTIC OCEAN' and the narration says it 'sits directly opposite the Arctic Ocean'.
issues.evidence: Frame 224.5: the yellow is the central basin only, and the pink area over Ellesmere, Baffin and Greenland plus the Taymyr and Severnaya Zemlya coast is larger than the yellow. Rasterized overlap of mirrored Antarctica: 37% inside the current polygon, 65% inside the marginal-seas union, 66% in ocean north of 68N, 67% over any ocean.
issues.fix: Use the same new Arctic polygon as above. As a backstop, change ch2.js section G to fill yellow = mirrored Antarctica minus land: clip mp to an ocean mask (inverse of ch2_landmask.png, or an even-odd path of ne_50m_land) instead of ctx.clip(ap). About two thirds of the shape then turns yellow and 'most' is visible.

issues.problem: A render glitch on the unplanned return flight north: the orange Antarctica fill is projected through the globe. An Antarctica-shaped orange blob sits on the Sahara and West Africa, then on France and Germany under the cyan shape, for ~1.4 s before the cut to the cut-away.
issues.evidence: Frames 214.6 (blob over West Africa) and 215.2 (blob over Central Europe). Cause: section E draw2d fills L.globePath(pj, antX, false) with clampHidden=false. Only the stroke (strokeGlobe) is horizon-culled.
issues.fix: In ch2.js section E, fill with L.globePath(pj, antX, true) and multiply that fill's alpha by (1 - prog(t, tBack, tBack + 0.35)) so Antarctica fades as the camera leaves. Or cut straight to the cut-away at tBack (~213.6) and drop the return flight.

issues.problem: A key proof beat is missing: the mirrored United States never appears (planned: cyan lower 48 in the Indian Ocean, Hawaii on Botswana, an Alaska sliver on Antarctica). On 'United States' the map zooms out to the world and back with nothing drawn except four specks off Brazil. The 'US AND CHINA: ZERO OVERLAP' pill and the JUICE CHECK FALSE stamp then assert a comparison the viewer never sees.
issues.evidence: Frames 264.6 and 265.7 show only orange China, the Kansas-antipode dot, and 4 white specks at ~15-20S 34W. Cause: ch2.js line 609 calls feat('United States of America'), and lib/geo.js findFeature also matches SOVEREIGNT. It therefore returns ne_50m_admin_0_countries feature 11, 'Northern Mariana Islands', whose antipodes are those specks; the USA is feature 16.
issues.fix: In ch2.js line 609 use const usF = feat('USA') (ISO_A3 match, unique). Optionally harden lib/geo.js findFeature to try ADMIN, NAME and ISO before SOVEREIGNT; no other ep01 lookup is affected today. Re-render 258-275 and check that the 263.3-264.4 flip lands the lower 48 around the Kansas-antipode marker.

issues.problem: Both cut-away shots (215.85-218.95 and 247.2-250.66) crop off the poles. The radius-3 Earth at ~8.2 units with fov 32 has a visible half-height of ~2.35. Viewers see an abstract orange 'heart' filling the frame: the drill enters from the top frame edge and exits off the bottom. The entry pulse (North Pole / Kansas) and exit pulse (Antarctica / Indian Ocean) drawn in code are off-screen, so 'through the core to the exact other side' has no geographic anchor, and the shape barely reads as Earth.
issues.evidence: Frames 218.6 and 249.0: no surface at the top or bottom of the cut. The projected top point (0,3,0) is ~20.6 deg off-axis against a 16 deg half-FOV.
issues.fix: ch2.js section F: change cam d from lerp(8.6,7.4) to lerp(12,11) and y from lerp(4.4,3.6) to lerp(5.4,4.8). Section J: change d from lerp(8.0,7.2) to lerp(11.5,10.5) and target y to 0 (or keep d and pass fov 46). The whole sphere then fits with ~8% margin, the cyan/yellow top pulse and orange bottom pulse become visible, and the textured shell frames the wedge.
issues.module: ch2 (ch2.js sections F and J, ch2_sets.js cutaway)

issues.problem: Three moves start exactly on their word with a slow inOut ease, so the visible motion trails the word instead of leading it. Drag: 'Drag' at 207.94, visible ~208.40 (+0.46 s). Drill: 'line up' at 217.64, visible ~217.97 (+0.33 s, while impact_deep hits at 217.61). Pull-back: 'poles' at 226.62, visible ~227.15 (+0.55 s).
issues.evidence: 30 fps tiles: the cyan shape is static through 208.33; the first drill head appears at 218.00; the overlay and camera are unchanged until ~227.1.
issues.fix: Section E dragState: prog(t, tm.drag - pre, tDragE, E.out). Section F: p = prog(t, tm.line - pre, tm.line + 1.0, E.out). Section G cam: k = prog(t, tm.poles - 0.4, tm.poles + 1.8, E.inOut).

issues.problem: Antimeridian and pole seam strokes. A straight white line runs from the cyan polygon's rim to the pole inside the 'Arctic Ocean'. An orange seam crosses Antarctica along 180 deg and through the yellow overlap. They read as cracks in the hero shapes.
issues.evidence: Frames 180.0 and 209.5 (white line inside the cyan), 212.5 (orange line from the bottom of the cyan to the Ross coast), 224.5 (line through the yellow).
issues.fix: Build stroke paths that skip segments whose two vertices both have |lon| >= 179.9 or |lat| >= 89.9 (in strokeGlobe and in section E's ctx.stroke(path)). Keep fills on the full ring. Applies to arcX, antX and antMirX, and still matters after the polygon swap because NE splits the Chukchi and East Siberian seas at 180.
issues.module: ch2 (ch2.js sections E, G; ch2_lib.js strokeGlobe)

issues.problem: Flat-map framing breaks the layout rules. In vIndian = eeViewAt(62,2,1.62) the Kansas-antipode marker sits at y~995, inside the bottom 12% under the YouTube controls, during the 'hemisphere' and stamp beats. China's northern tip touches the top edge, and the 'US AND CHINA: ZERO OVERLAP' pill sits on top of China. Once the US mirror renders, the lower 48 (25-49S) would also fall off the bottom.
issues.evidence: Frames 260.2 (marker at y=993) and 265.7 (marker at y=1000, pill over Inner Mongolia).
issues.fix: Set vIndian = L.eeViewAt(82, -4, 1.2). Computed positions: China top y~91, marker y~828, bottom of the mirrored lower 48 y~892, Hawaii antipode (592,682). Anchor the pill left at x~140, y~110 over Africa/Europe.

issues.problem: The counting ruler number ('0.9' up to '1.8 MI') is white text on the near-white ice and becomes unreadable as the ice rises. The thickness bracket on 'thick' is a thin, unlabeled, low-contrast cyan line. The 'SOUTH POLE: NEARLY 2 MILES UP' pill's right edge (~1855 px) is outside the 5% title-safe margin (1824 px).
issues.evidence: Frame 197.8.
issues.fix: Draw the ruler number in navy #0b1730, or on a small dark pill to the right of the ruler. Make the bracket 6 px with a dark outline. Shift the pill ~50 px left.

issues.problem: EXPLORER GAG 3 (vertigo over 2.5 miles of water) does not read. HitRecieve_2 plays as a ~0.15 s head flinch on a ~270 px figure in a locked wide shot, and he never looks down. The panel then sits near-static from 188.1 to 190.7.
issues.evidence: Explorer crops 187.5-189.0: only 188.05-188.2 show a slight head tilt.
issues.fix: At tm.depth+0.6 scale the composited Explorer 1.0 to 1.5 about his feet (or push the camera in) and play HitRecieve_2 at speed 0.7 with fade 0.08. Add a 3-frame camera shake and a cartoon_fall sting before the whip.

issues.problem: During the pop-out jump the 'INDIAN OCEAN' pill is drawn across the Explorer's chest, and his head is clipped by the top frame edge.

issues.fix: Section K: fade the pill in at tm.indian + 0.9, after the Roll lands. Or lower the jump apex (moveAlong y +0.4 to +0.25) so his head stays below y~200.

issues.problem: The dig reads as a lightsaber. A glowing blue rod hangs from his hand to the ground while he stands in Idle_Neutral, then he sinks upright like an elevator. The weapon-like look conflicts with the no-weapons rule.
issues.evidence: Frame 246.3.
issues.fix: Start the beam at the ground under his feet as a glowing hole with a dirt fountain (dig_shovel cue). Keep him in Interact/crouch, and drop him with a short hop and a cartoon_fall cue instead of sinking upright.

issues.problem: The Kerguelen Islands sit in the lower-left foreground as a large bright-white landmass, while the pill says '200+ MILES TO THE NEAREST LAND' and points at a tiny dot. Perspective makes Kerguelen (~900 mi away) look like the nearest land.
issues.evidence: Frame 257.0: white island at (420,1010) against the Saint-Paul dot at (845,327).
issues.fix: Section L: rotate the camera heading ~40 deg to look north-west so Kerguelen leaves the frame, or radially dim the texture beyond ~800 km from the antipode.

issues.problem: After the pull-back the frame is a plain Europe/Africa globe for ~5 s with only a 1.5 s overlay. The flipped-land glimpse sits foreshortened on the left limb, so 'land has ocean on its far side' is barely shown.
issues.evidence: Frames 228.5-233.3. At 230.5 the cyan flipped Australia is on the left limb.

issues.problem: The chimney smoke on the houseboat diorama is a column of perfectly round, flat translucent discs that reads as bubbles. It stays on screen for the whole 6 s gag.
issues.evidence: Frame 183.2.
issues.fix: Use soft radial-gradient puffs with random size and offset jitter that grow and fade as they rise.
